# ferentin_endpoint_sandbox (Resource)

The tenant's agent sandbox policy: which AI tools on managed devices have Ferentin's sandbox written into their native sandbox settings, the folders their commands may write or must not touch, and the domains they may reach. **One per tenant.**

Every value is checked with the device's own grammar; a value devices would refuse is refused at plan where the provider can tell, and by the platform (a 400 naming the field) otherwise. A change reaches devices on the tenant's next policy activation.

Claude Code, Codex and Copilot read a managed file the developer cannot switch off (`reach = "enforced"`). Cursor and Antigravity read the sandbox only from the developer's own settings, so there it is a default the developer can undo (`reach = "default_only"`).

~> **Destroy** saves a policy that enables no tool (the platform has no delete): Ferentin stops writing the sandbox into every tool's settings, and the folders and domains are cleared.

## Import

Create refuses to overwrite a policy the tenant already saved. Import it instead:

```
terraform import ferentin_endpoint_sandbox.this <tenant_id>
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The agent sandbox: what AI coding tools' shell commands may write, must not
# touch and may reach on managed devices. One per tenant.
resource "ferentin_endpoint_sandbox" "this" {
  tools = {
    # Enforced: a managed file the developer cannot switch off.
    "claude-code" = { enabled = true }
    "codex"       = { enabled = true }
    # Docker and similar need to run outside the sandbox; let the tool's own
    # approval prompt allow that rather than switching the sandbox off.
    "copilot" = { enabled = true, allow_unsandboxed = true }
    # A default only: Cursor reads the sandbox from the developer's settings.
    "cursor" = { enabled = true }
  }

  # Omit this block to keep the devices' credential template (~/.ssh, ~/.aws,
  # ~/.gnupg, ~/.config/gh, ~/Library/Keychains). Set, it is taken as written,
  # so restate the template if you still want it.
  filesystem = {
    writable = ["~/.cache/pip", "/opt/build-cache"]
    denied   = ["~/.ssh", "~/.aws", "~/.gnupg", "~/.config/gh", "~/Library/Keychains", "~/secrets"]
  }

  allowed_domains = ["registry.npmjs.org", "pypi.org", "*.githubusercontent.com"]

  # Also allow what the tenant already allows elsewhere: unconditioned allow
  # destination rules, approved MCP servers and the Ferentin gateway.
  include_derived_domains = true

  description = "Coding agents: package registries only"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `allowed_domains` (Set of String) Domains sandboxed commands may reach: a DNS name of two or more labels, optionally `*.`-prefixed for its subdomains. No port, scheme, IP address or bare `*`. At most 256. Empty or unset means no network, unless `include_derived_domains` adds some.

The platform trims, lowercases and strips trailing dots; Terraform keeps your spelling here and the platform's in `stored_allowed_domains`.
- `description` (String) Free-form admin note. Never reaches the device. At most 500 characters.
- `filesystem` (Attributes) Folders sandboxed commands may write or must not touch. **Omit the block** to keep the devices' credential template: they deny `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.config/gh` and `~/Library/Keychains` (see `default_denied_paths`) and allow nothing extra writable. Present, it is taken as written. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filesystem))
- `include_derived_domains` (Boolean) Also allow the hosts the tenant already allows elsewhere: unconditioned allow destination rules, approved MCP servers and the Ferentin gateway. Derived hosts come after yours and are cut first if the list would pass 256. Default `true`.
- `tenant_id` (String)
- `tools` (Attributes Map) Per AI tool, keyed by the hook vendor's name: `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `antigravity`. A tool absent from the map, or with `enabled = false`, is left to whoever else manages its sandbox. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `default_denied_paths` (List of String) Read-only. What devices deny while no `filesystem` block is set. Null when one is.
- `id` (String) The tenant id: there is one sandbox policy per tenant.
- `last_modified_by` (String) Provenance of the most recent writer. Divergence from `managed_by` is the drift signal.
- `managed_by` (String) Provenance of the original creator (`iac` for this provider).
- `managed_by_client_id` (String)
- `managed_by_module` (String)
- `policy_id` (String)
- `stored_allowed_domains` (Set of String) Read-only. `allowed_domains` as the platform stores them, normalized.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version` (Number) Optimistic-concurrency version, sent as `If-Match` on update and destroy so a concurrent console edit is rejected with 412 rather than overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--filesystem"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filesystem`

Required:

- `denied` (Set of String) Folders commands may neither read nor write. Required in the block; an empty set denies nothing (not even the credential template). At most 64.

Optional:

- `writable` (Set of String) Folders commands may write besides the project and the temporary directory, which are always writable. Absolute (`/opt/cache`) or home-relative (`~/scratch`). At most 64. Refused: a home folder, a `Library` or `LaunchAgents` folder, `/var/root`, an agent's or editor's settings folder, and a folder inside a denied one.


<a id="nestedatt--tools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether Ferentin writes the sandbox into this tool's settings.

Optional:

- `allow_unsandboxed` (Boolean) The escape hatch. `false` (the default) is strict: the tool may not retry a command outside the sandbox and the developer may not switch it off. `true` keeps the sandbox on and lets the tool's own approval prompt run a command outside it (Docker and similar). On Codex, `false` also restricts the approval policy to never.

Read-Only:

- `reach` (String) Read-only. `enforced` (a managed file the developer cannot switch off) or `default_only` (a default in the developer's own settings).
